profiled_workloads.selection_reason: lowest speedup and smallest shape: 1024 fp16 with one program isolates per-call host cost from kernel work; cheapest case for instruction listing
1M fp16: its 34-40us kernel still fits inside the flat 75us floor, the decisive case for the host versus device split
highest latency fp16 4096x4096 with 16384 programs: the only device-bound regime
4096x4096 fp32: same element count with twice the bytes, so equal latency separates bandwidth limits from instruction-issue limits

findings.label: per-call host launch gap dominates every workload up to 1M elements

evidence.metric: kernel median duration vs inter-launch interval median
kernel duration vs inter-launch interval (1M fp16)

findings.inference: Device execution is only about 2 percent of the 75us walltime for 1024 elements, and the kernel for 1M elements (34-40us) still fits inside the same 75us floor. The flat floor across 1K and 1M elements proves a per-call host cost, not element work.

findings.label: 4096x4096 case is scalar/issue bound, not MTE bandwidth bound

evidence.metric: kernel duration fp16 vs fp32 at 2x bytes

findings.inference: DMA engines are idle about 85 percent of the kernel and doubling moved bytes adds only 2us, so the 16384-program kernel is not MTE bandwidth bound. The instruction listing shows roughly 190 mapped instructions per 1024-element program with only about 30 vector operations and repeated per-block barrier and flag stalls, so issue/scalar work dominates.

performance_interpretation: Nine of the twelve timing workloads sit at a 75-87us host-side floor while their kernels run only 1.3-40us, so their measured speedups (0.13-0.16) are set by per-call dispatch overhead against an 11.2-12.8us torch reference. The three 4096x4096 cases are device-bound near 600us with scalar ratio 0.59-0.66, vector ratio 0.13-0.18 and MTE ratios 0.12-0.16, i.e. an instruction-issue limit in a 16384-program grid of 1024-element blocks rather than a memory limit. Effective bandwidth computed from eval latency and algorithmic bytes is about 112 GB/s for fp16 and 223 GB/s for fp32, far below any plausible HBM ceiling and not a Roofline claim.

next_experiment.action_description: Keep BLOCK_SIZE=1024 and all math unchanged: wrap selu_kernel_ with @libentry() from flag_gems.utils.libentry (caches the compiled kernel and launches kernel[grid](*args), bypassing JITFunction.run after the first call), replace the lambda grid with a precomputed tuple ((n+1023)//1024,), and drop the per-call torch_device_fn.device context and logger.debug from the hot path.
next_experiment.expected_impact: If python dispatch and device guarding account for the 63us excess over the 11.6us reference, the small and medium walltime floor drops from 75us toward 30-45us (geo_mean 0.13 to 0.20-0.30); the three device-bound 4096x4096 cases stay unchanged within 5 percent.
next_experiment.risks_and_rollback: LibEntry requires the grid= keyword and triton 3.3-3.6 (3.5.1 is installed); rollback by restoring @triton.jit with the lambda grid. Do not change block size this round so the measurement stays causal. Keep in-place semantics and the strided fallback untouched.

1024, 65536 and 1048576 element workloads below 60us (speedup at least 0.19) for fp16, bf16 and fp32

warnings: msprof and simulator timings are diagnostic only; eval latency remains authoritative
the launch-gap attribution to specific host components is not resolvable from these artifacts
the 4096x4096 per-invocation duration spread (511-704us) is unexplained and must not be treated as a stable kernel cost
open_questions: Which host component accounts for the roughly 63us excess over the reference (triton dispatch, device guard, or ACL launch) cannot be separated with the collected artifacts because the msprof host collection exported no API summary.

Whether a larger BLOCK_SIZE would cut the 0.63 scalar share on the 4096x4096 cases is unverified; the instruction mix suggests at most a 1.3-2x gain because most scalar instructions scale with vector operations.
The 4096x4096 kernel duration is bimodal (511-704us) with zero device wait time; the cause (clock/power state) cannot be attributed from the available counters.
